summary: Lincoln County, MT lookout on the Kootenai NF: frame cabin 1921, 10-foot pole L-4 tower 1942, destroyed about 1975; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: frame cabin (1921), then a 10-foot wood pole tower with L-4 cab (1942)

events.note: 10-foot wood pole tower with L-4 cab

evidence.supports: frame cabin 1921; 10-foot pole L-4 tower 1942; destroyed 1975
evidence.quote: 1921: frame cabin. 1942: 10' pole L-4 tower. Destroyed 1975.

evidence.supports: peakbagging.com name Roderick Mountain; elevation 6,635 feet for the mountain
evidence.quote: Roderick Mountain, Lincoln County, Montana, Elevation = 6635 ft.

evidence.supports: lookout on a small hill about 700 feet southwest of the high point
evidence.quote: The lookout was on a small hill 700 ft. to the southwest.
This is the highest point of Roderick Mountain which has the benchmark.
Roderick ET benchmark was placed in 1963.

evidence.supports: 10-foot wood pole tower with L-4 cab built 1942
evidence.quote: A 10 ft. wood pole tower with L-4 cab was constructed in 1942.

evidence.supports: page has a photo dated 2020; text does not say what it shows

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com gives 6,600 feet for the lookout. Peakbagging.com gives 6,635 feet for Roderick Mountain itself. The record uses 6,600 because it is the lookout's own figure; the story says which source gives which number.
Firelookout.com gives the destruction year as 1975 and peakbagging.com says about 1975. Both are kept as one date, with the difference stated in the event note.

notes_for_editor: Two independent pages agree on the 1942 pole tower and the mid-1970s destruction. The 1921 frame cabin appears only on firelookout.com. Peakbagging.com describes the lookout as 700 feet southwest of the high point, which has a benchmark placed 1963 (datasheet TN0949); it does not say whether the benchmark is still there today. Staffing, fires, access and visit details were not found in any source, so they are left out. Peakbagging.com has a photo dated August 10, 2020, but no image URL was found, so no photo is added. The second search turned up the peakbagging page; nothing else was found.
